title: Test title still labels the bin-play timing question OPEN after a ruling answered it
summary: A 12-fire-a test title marks "a bin-played card obeys its PRINTED timing" as an open question. The owner ruling of 2026-08-26 (“an option list is not "any…”) records that the owner ruling of 2026-08-25 (“the owner's answers to the 27…”) ruled a bin-play grant does not waive printed timing, which is what the test asserts. The behaviour is settled; only the title (and the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“Playing a spell from your BIN…”)’s own "OPEN" heading) still reads as undecided. A test-title fix, not an engine bug.

title: Three test titles claim more than their tests assert
summary: Each title names a behaviour the body never checks. The 12-fire-a Abyssal Evocation test says "until regroup" ends the stamp but never reaches regroup. The 403 the owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“A copy is read by its…”) test says the Borrower dies to the bin but never kills it (26-metal-a's the owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“A copy is read by its…”) test does). The owner ruling of 2026-08-19 (“Prophecy conditions count forward from the…”) "One Battle Passes" title says both battles tick, but the test counts only one round. Each needs an assertion added or its title narrowed. These are test problems, not engine bugs: the round-1 verifier measured the engine and it agrees.
